title: Resurrection of the Dead
lead: The hope that God will raise the dead to life in the body. Most of the Old Testament pictures the dead in Sheol, and only a few late or disputed passages speak of rising again; by the time of Jesus many Jews, especially the Pharisees, believed in a resurrection at the end of days, and the New Testament proclaims that it has begun with the resurrection of Jesus.

sections.b: Much of the Hebrew Bible pictures the dead going down to Sheol, a place of silence and dust from which no one returns (Job 7:9–10; Psalm 88:10–12; Ecclesiastes 9:5, 10). God's power over death is affirmed (Deuteronomy 32:39; 1 Samuel 2:6), and prophets raise individual children (1 Kings 17:17–24; 2 Kings 4:32–37), but a general rising of the dead is not taught in the Law or the early histories.
sections.refs: Job 7:9–10; Psalm 88:10–12; Ecclesiastes 9:5; Deuteronomy 32:39; 1 Samuel 2:6; 1 Kings 17:17–24; 2 Kings 4:32–37

sections.b: Some passages reach beyond death: the psalmist's hope that God will not leave him in Sheol (Psalm 16:10; Psalm 49:15; Psalm 73:24), Ezekiel's valley of dry bones, a picture of the nation's revival (Ezekiel 37:1–14), and Isaiah's 'your dead will live' (Isaiah 26:19). Daniel 12:2 is the clearest statement: many who sleep in the dust will wake, some to everlasting life and some to shame. Job 19:25–27 is the most debated case: the Greek and Latin translations and most Christian readers find a resurrection there, while many modern scholars read it as a hope for vindication.
sections.refs: Psalm 16:10; Psalm 49:15; Psalm 73:24; Ezekiel 37:1–14; Isaiah 26:19; Daniel 12:2; Job 19:25–27

sections.b: In Jesus' time the Pharisees believed in a resurrection and the Sadducees did not (Acts 23:6–8); Jesus answers the Sadducees from the Torah (Mark 12:18–27). The New Testament's central claim is that God raised Jesus bodily from the dead, the firstfruits of a general resurrection to come (1 Corinthians 15:3–8, 20–23). Paul describes the raised body as imperishable and spiritual, yet still a body (1 Corinthians 15:35–54).
sections.refs: Acts 23:6–8; Mark 12:18–27; 1 Corinthians 15:3–8; 1 Corinthians 15:20–23; 1 Corinthians 15:35–54; John 11:23–26
